content.thinking:
I'm planning the elephant's skeleton structure, designing a hip root joint with a spine chain running forward to the shoulders and neck, plus a separate chain for the trunk, all scaled to a bush elephant's proportions facing forward.

For the head and body, I'm positioning a large head joint near the spine's tip and defining a body sweep path running from rump to chest, attaching it to the hips and spine bones so the geometry follows the skeleton correctly.

Now I'm defining the barrel radius profile for a round, elephant-like body shape and setting up the skin paint with a mottled gray base plus countershading and wrinkle-like stripes along the body axis.

Working out body placement: axis height around 2.1-2.2 with belly clearance so the bottom sits near 1.2 and the top near 3.0, matching the target shoulder height. Then I'm positioning the front legs symmetrically, placing shoulder and foot joints and leg segment lengths for each side.

I need the foot cap to not dip below the floor, so I should set the target y to match the radius so the rounded bottom lands right at zero, adjusting for how far the sphere cap extends past the path endpoint.

I'll switch to a flat end cap instead of round for the foot, picking a small target y near 0.05 and tapering the tube radius down to 0.3, then checking the limb lengths against the distance from root to target so the leg bends naturally forward at the knee.

For feet, I'm adding a flattened cylinder pad near the ground with a dark color, plus a row of toenail boxes along the front edge in a cream tone, attaching them to the foot joint at the end of the leg chain.

Now for the head, I'm shaping it as a scaled sphere positioned near the top of the body, stretching it wider and taller to match elephant proportions, with plans to add forehead and cheek detail next.

Then I'm adding a jaw as a small frustum attached below the head, and setting up the trunk as a multi-joint tentacle chain hanging forward from the head with a gentle curl toward the tip, tapering its radius along the way with ridge detailing.

I'm adding striped wrinkle rings along the trunk's skin texture, making sure the tip clears the floor with a rounded cap, and giving it a small nostril cone at the end. I also need to make sure the trunk's root joint anchors properly inside the head before moving on to sweeping the tusks as curved bezier paths from the jaw area.

For the tusks, I'm defining a cubic bezier curve that bends down then forward, tapering the radius from a flat base to a pointed ivory tip, and considering a small ring detail at the base. Now I'm shifting to the ears, planning to extrude their outline shape in a side-facing plane to get the characteristic large, flat form.

Adding thin ear bones with hinge joints, then setting up a paint function to shade the ears darker at the tips with mottled coloring elsewhere.

For the inner ear, I'm blending a pinkish tone based on position so it reads as the softer inner surface without going overboard on detail. Then I'm moving to the eyes, placing small dark spheres on the sides of the head with an amber ring for the iris, keeping the brow simple.

For the tail, I'm chaining it as a series of jointed points from the rump downward, tapering the radius as it goes, then adding a fan of dark spike cones at the tip to give it a tufted end.

Now I'm layering surface details onto the body: wrinkle stripes running along the z-axis with some wobble for a worn, leathery texture, plus gradient dust paint fading up the legs to suggest mud caking near the feet.

I'm also composing a countershaded belly-to-back color blend nested with mottling, then stacking wrinkle stripes on top, and planning a lower jaw piece built from a frustum box near the mouth.

Now I'm sketching out the shoulder and haunch masses as scaled spheres tied to spine joints, using the skin paint on them, and adding small forehead and cheek domes near the skull.

For the neck, I'm connecting the body to the head with a sweep between two points, parenting it to the last spine joint, and then working out how the front legs should also parent off that last joint in the spine chain.

Now I'm sketching out the torso shape, defining a radius function that bulges and tapers along its length to give the body a rounded, tapered silhouette, checking the resulting dimensions at the midpoint.

Still placing joints...
